headline: Shifts Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the direct costs of their required grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for Power Lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these billions of dollars in expenses from falling on residential ratepayers. This decision is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars and was supported by Governor Abigail Spanberger.

headline: Mandates Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report the monthly water consumption of data centers, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact and aiding water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates local water authorities to publicly report data center water usage, aiming to provide transparency and inform public discourse on the industry's environmental impact. The data will be aggregated and available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website, with an effective date of January 1, 2027.

headline: Establishes Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor‑Chapter 567 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: Data Centers May Need Noise, Energy Disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, high energy use facilities (100 MW or more), primarily data centers, will trigger special-exception submission requirements in Fairfax County, including a mandatory noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet. Additionally, applicants must provide a statement from their energy provider detailing anticipated demand and energy source.
